title: First Unique Letter in a Name
statement: Given a string name, return the first letter that appears exactly once. Ignore case. If none exists, return null.
think: What is the task asking? Find the first letter whose count is exactly one.
What is the key operation? Count frequencies first, then preserve the original order in a second pass.
What wording signals stand out? First unique, appears once, count letters.
What is the brute force idea? For each character, count its occurrences by rescanning the whole string.
What is the better/optimal idea? Two passes with a frequency map.
What are the edge cases? No unique letters, mixed case, spaces.
What is the complexity? O(n) time and O(k) space.
How would I explain it in an interview? I first count all letters, then scan the string again to find the first one whose count is one.
algorithm: First pass: count each letter in lower case
Second pass: return the first letter whose count is 1
interview: I would use a frequency map and two passes. The first pass counts letters, and the second pass returns the first one whose count is exactly one.
ru: Это задача на частоты и порядок. Сначала считаем все буквы, потом снова идём по строке и находим первую с count == 1.
visualExplanation:

critical: Use HashSet and lose frequency information
important: Forget the second pass and lose the first position
nice: Do not explain why order matters after counting

gaps: Important: understand frequency + second scan pattern
Nice to have: distinguish first unique from first repeated
constraints: Assume the input is a short name string.
whyThisPattern: This is a Dictionary problem because we need per-letter counts before we can identify the first unique character.
whyNotOtherPatterns: Not HashSet, because HashSet does not store frequencies.
Not Two Pointers, because this is not a left/right comparison problem.
